page: Amazon Web Services r8i.8xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 32 vCPUs derived from 16 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor running at 3.9 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes a 480 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and 8-bit integer operations. The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core. Local storage is not bundled with this instance, and network connectivity is established via a 15 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong performance in single-threaded and multi-threaded operations. The instance achieved a Geekbench single-core score of 2043.0 and a multi-core score of 17097.0, both falling into the strong performance tier. Single-threaded gzip compression reached 33.51 GB/sec, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression registered at 223.94 GB/sec. In memory bandwidth testing, the server recorded 133.67 GB/sec for large block read-only operations and 63.0 GB/sec for large block write operations. Cryptographic performance is also notable, with a Passmark CPU encryption score of 36285.59.

For machine learning workloads, the hardware demonstrates a clear performance tradeoff based on model size. While text generation for a small 135M parameter LLM model reaches a top-tier speed of 404.39 tokens/sec, performance drops to a weak 2.71 tokens/sec for text generation with a large 70B parameter model. This makes the instance highly suitable for smaller-scale model inference, in-memory database operations, and memory-intensive data processing, but less optimal for large-scale LLM text generation. The high memory-to-vCPU ratio provides qualitative cost efficiency for workloads requiring substantial RAM without the overhead of excess compute cores.
